data.description:
## Purpose

One-time reclaim of the ~1 GiB already spent on the `tickets` branch (the sibling code
levers under this epic bound *future* growth; this ticket reclaims the *existing* bloat), plus
the tickets-store git maintenance that can only run safely when no other session is writing to
the branch. Bundled here because both operations require the same **quiet maintenance window**
and must be executed by the session that owns this epic. Another session is coordinating that
window; this ticket is the handoff.

## Why a quiet window is required

The tickets store auto-commits and auto-pushes every ticket write to `origin/tickets`. History
rewrite / aggressive repack while other agents are writing will race (non-fast-forward pushes,
lost writes, or a corrupted local view). Execute ONLY after the coordinating session confirms
all parallel sessions have paused ticket writes for the duration.

## Git maintenance (the reclaim)

Against a fresh, exclusive clone of `origin` (never the shared main checkout, which may hold
uncommitted operator WIP):

1. Snapshot/backup the current `origin/tickets` ref (record the SHA on this ticket) before any
   rewrite so the operation is reversible.
2. Aggressive repack to recover delta compression defeated by the scattered `.bridge_state`
   edits: `git repack -ad --window=250 --depth=50` (+ `git gc --prune=now`). Measure branch
   size before/after. If repack alone does not reclaim enough, evaluate a history filter of the
   spent `.bridge_state` churn per the epic's research (session_log 1cb6-d553-6565-49b4) — but
   only with explicit human sign-off, since it rewrites `tickets` history and force-updates the
   shared ref.
3. Force-update `origin/tickets` (fast-forward if possible; a rewrite requires the window +
   sign-off) and have every active checkout re-fetch/reset its tickets tracking ref afterward.

## Coordinate with the fsck remediation

Run inside the SAME window as / immediately before-or-after ticket 30d3-eaf0-c7a4-497a
(remediate 561 fsck diagnostics). Both mutate store integrity; sequencing them together avoids
a second window. Order: repair fsck diagnostics (30d3) first so the store is clean, then repack.
Record the interleave actually used on both tickets.

## Handoff to the receiving session (epic owner: 0303 / REB-1654)

- Pre-flight: confirm all parallel sessions have paused ticket writes (coordinating session
  gives the go signal); record the `origin/tickets` SHA here as the rollback point.
- Do NOT run in the shared /Users/joeoakhart/rebar checkout — use a throwaway exclusive clone.
- Read the epic's research trail (session_log 1cb6-d553-6565-49b4) for the measured 12.79 KB ->
  1.74 KB marginal-cost figures and the repack parameters that produced them.
- After the window: verify `rebar fsck` is clean, record before/after branch sizes and the new
  `origin/tickets` SHA on this ticket, then signal parallel sessions to resume writes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Quiet-window pre-flight (writes paused, rollback SHA recorded) is completed and logged here.
- [ ] Tickets-store git maintenance (repack/gc, and any sanctioned history filter) is executed
      against an exclusive clone; before/after branch sizes are recorded on this ticket.
- [ ] Coordinated with 30d3 in the same window; the execution order is recorded on both tickets.
- [ ] `origin/tickets` is updated and all active checkouts re-sync; new SHA recorded here.
- [ ] Post-window `rebar fsck` reports clean and the reclaimed size is quantified against the
      ~1 GiB target.
data.title: Quiet-window reclaim of the spent ~1 GiB + tickets-store git maintenance (handoff)
